answer: The meadow test I would run is Proof of unique archaeological dig permit: a permit held for one site across three seasons, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. What makes this stick is that a permit held for one site across three seasons cannot be faked in bulk — each proof is independent, and the nebula of independence is that one compromised proof endangers no other account. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the nectar of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out.
